Q: Read and display milliseconds A:

Using your original readr::read_tsv approach, use locale=, e.g.

library(readr)

read_tsv("date_time", 
         locale = locale(date_format = "%m/%d/%Y", 
                         time_format = "%I:%M:%OS %p")
)

Q: Sandbox account does not appear in the app store section in settings A:

​In iOS 18.*, the location of the Sandbox Account setting has changed. To access it:​

Open the Settings ->​ Developer -> Scroll to the bottom to find the Sandbox section.​

If you don't see the Developer option in Settings, you may need to enable Developer Mode:​

Go to Settings -> Privacy & Security. Scroll down and tap on Developer Mode to turn it on and follow the above instructions to find Sandbox Section.

Q: How to correctly apply causal masking in Keras Multi-Head Attention for multi-step time series forecasting? A:

MultiHeadAttention already has causal masking built in, so there is no need to create the triangular mask manually:

def call(self, inputs, training=False):
    attn_output = self.att(
        query=inputs,
        value=inputs,
        key=inputs,
        use_causal_mask=True,
        training=training,
    )

    attn_output = self.dropout1(attn_output, training=training)
    out1 = self.layernorm1(inputs + attn_output)

    ffn_output = self.ffn(out1)
    ffn_output = self.dropout2(ffn_output, training=training)

    return self.layernorm2(out1 + ffn_output)

This also works with a dynamic sequence length.

If you do build the mask yourself, (sequence_length, sequence_length) is sufficient. Keras broadcasts it across the batch and attention heads:

sequence_length = tf.shape(inputs)[1]

mask = tf.linalg.band_part(
    tf.ones(
        (sequence_length, sequence_length),
        dtype=tf.bool,
    ),
    -1,
    0,
)

attn_output = self.att(
    query=inputs,
    value=inputs,
    key=inputs,
    attention_mask=mask,
    training=training,
)

Looking at the model description, though, the encoder may not need this mask. If inputs contains only historical values available at the forecast origin, allowing those positions to attend to each other does not introduce target leakage.

The causal mask matters when previous target values are fed into an autoregressive decoder, or when the prediction at position t must not see positions after t.

Also check how the training windows are constructed. A causal mask will not prevent leakage if future target or climate values are already included in inputs.

See the MultiHeadAttention documentation for the accepted mask shapes and use_causal_mask.

Q: Something unusual has occurred to cause the driver to fail. Heroku postgresql database A:

My first guess would be a malformed connection string. Are you using a proper JDBC URL (i.e. it starts with jdbc:) for dbUrl? Also make sure you include sslmode=require.

In addition, please be aware that the database URL is managed by Heroku and will change under certain circumstances. You can read more about using Heroku Postgres from outside of Heroku in this DevCenter article.

Q: Missing expression after unary operator '-'. At line:1 char:2 A:

At the end I am able to crack the issue and it was very difficult to find. Our administartor copied/pasted the command line for NSC.ini file from a MS-Word document (How To doc.) shared by me to them. In the original MS-Word doc the hypen (at the end of the line after the word command in the beow given command line) has automatically changed to a little bigger hypen during documentation, which also gone to the NSC.ini file and hence the error was coming for this particular command execution. After changing the hypen manually in the NSC.ini, it worked fine without any issues

Q: InfoPath Forms Services is not turned on A:

  2. Tick the check box "Enable all sites..."
